title: a worker session opens its item's work window without a second claim, so backlog cost counts its prompts
goal: a headless worker session opens the work window of the item it works with backlog.py claim ID --resume by the claimer's name (no second claim commit, no status change), and backlog.py cost ID then counts that session's prompts instead of reading 0. Answers the SP-sz5fbvqn retrospective: the Sonnet worker sessions loaded the hooks but never ran claim (the orchestrator claimed in its own session), so no window opened and every item's cost read 0 although the sessions cost about 4.4 USD in all (kb/_self/usage.md, a window needs a claim the session itself ran).

run: import subprocess,sys;p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/backlog.py','claim','-h'],capture_output=True,text=True);ok='--resume' in p.stdout;print('claim -h offers --resume:',ok);sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

notes: Premise: no check planted. The mechanism is open (claim --resume or a window row at the worker's first command), and the end state needs a spool of a real session's rows; a check written before that choice would pin one design. Evidence: backlog.py cost reads 0 for every SP-sz5fbvqn item although the worker sessions ran.
